root_cause.text: In dm-mpath's parse_path() error handling, the newly added failure path for scsi_dh_attached_handler_name() returning an error exited via bad without releasing the just-acquired p->path.dev reference, causing a device reference leak.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states it "didn't clean up the reference to the path device that had just been taken," and the patch changes the PTR_ERR(attached_handler_name) path from `goto bad;` to `goto bad_put_device;`, adding `dm_put_device(ti, p->path.dev);` before freeing the pgpath.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix parse_path() error handling to release the acquired device on all relevant failures and report handler-name allocation errors explicitly.
intent_record.what: The error path in parse_path() was reorganized by replacing several direct 'goto bad' branches with 'goto bad_put_device', adding a new bad_put_device label that calls dm_put_device(ti, p->path.dev) before falling through to the existing bad label, and setting ti->error to "error allocating handler name" when attached_handler_name allocation fails.
intent_record.how: This ensures the device reference acquired for p->path.dev is released on all failure paths after device setup has succeeded, including handler-name allocation failure, setup_scsi_dh() failure, and add_path() failure, while also providing a specific error message for handler-name allocation errors; at runtime it prevents leaked device references during parse failures.

grouping_result.intent: Fix parse_path() error handling to release the acquired device on all relevant failures and report handler-name allocation errors explicitly.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly targets parse_path() error handling by ensuring the acquired p->path.dev reference is released on failure paths, including the scsi_dh_attached_handler_name() error case that caused the device reference leak described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This error-path jump is the direct cause of the leak described in the root cause: when scsi_dh_attached_handler_name() returns an error, execution goes to bad without first releasing the already acquired p->path.dev reference.
The bad label only frees the pgpath structure and does not drop the device reference, so reaching this statement from the new handler-name error path leaves p->path.dev leaked.

vuln_statements.explanation: This jump is taken when scsi_dh_attached_handler_name() returns an error after p->path.dev has already been acquired. It transfers control to the bad path without releasing that device reference, directly causing the reference leak.

This cleanup at the bad label frees only the pgpath structure. Because it does not release p->path.dev, any path reaching this statement from the handler-name error case leaks the acquired device reference.
